title_ar: الشيخ الددو: الحج ارتبط بالسياسة منذ فرضه
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew: The Hajj Has Been Bound Up With Politics Since It Was Made Obligatory
body_ar:
قال فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو إن الحج ارتبط بالسياسة منذ فرضه في السنة التاسعة من الهجرة، مضيفا أن الحج هو أكبر مؤتمر يجمع المسلمين، يجتمع فيه قاصيهم ودانيهم ومشرقيُهم ومغربيُهم وعربيُهم وعجميُهم، يلتقون على كلمة سواء وهي كلمة التوحيد الموحدة لصفوف المسلمين جميعا.

وقال الشيخ خلال مقابلة له اليوم الثلاثاء 15/10/2013 مع قناة الجزيرة الفضائية من مشعر "منى" إن السياسة لا يمكن فصلها عن الحج بحال من الأحوال، ففيه نزلت سورة "براءه" وهي سورة مليئة بالأحكام السياسية.

موضحا أن السياسة نوعان، منها ما هو من الدين وهذا لا يُفصل عن الحج بحال من الأحوال؛ كالمواقف التي أمر الله بها، فقد قال الله تعالى {وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان واتقوا الله} وكالكلام عن تحرير المسجد الأقصى وعن إنكار الإبادة الجماعية للشعب السوري، وغير ذلك من الامور التي هي موقف شرعي وهي في نفس الوقت موقف سياسي بحت.

ومنها ما هو سلبي مما يؤدي إلى الخلافات والنزاعات والفوضى بين المسلمين في أمور هم في غنى عنها؛ وهذا هو المحذور.

وهذا نص مقابلة الشيخ: 

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم 

الحمد لله رب العالمين وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين 

الحج هو أكبر مؤتمر يجمع المسلمين، يجتمع فيه قاصيهم ودانيهم ومشرقيُهم ومغربيُهم وعربيُهم وعجميُهم، يلتقون على كلمة سواء وهي كلمة التوحيد الموحدة لصوف المسلمين جميعا.

والسياسة نوعان، منها ما هو من الدين وهذا لا يُفصل عن الحج بحال من الأحوال؛ كالمواقف التي أمر الله بها، فقد قال الله تعالى {وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا الإثم والعدوان واتقوا الله} وكالكلام عن تحرير المسجد الأقصى وعن إنكار الإبادة الجماعية للشعب السوري، وغير ذلك من الامور التي هي موقف شرعي وهي في نفس الموقت موقف سياسي.

ومنها ما هو سلبي مما يؤدي إلى الخلافات والنزاع والفوضى بين المسلمين في أمور هم في غنى عنها؛ وهذا هو المحذور. 

ولذلك فالحج ارتبط بالسياسة منذ فرضه، فقد فُرض الحج في العام التاسع من الهجرة، وأرسل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا بكر الصديق أميرا على الحج، فنزلت سورة "براءة" وكلها أحكام سياسية.

فأمر رسول الله علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أن يبلغ عنه في الحج، فخرج في علي في أثر أبي بكر وبلغ عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المشاعر وفي عرفة وعند البيت الحرام. 

وقد سئل علي رضي الله عنه بم بعثك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرفع يده فقال بأربعة أمور: 

- الأمر الأول أنه لا يدخل الجنة إلا نفس مؤمنة 

- والأمر الثاني أن لا يطوف بالبيت عُريان 

- والامر الثالث من كان بينه وبين رسول الله عهد فعهده إلا مدته 

- والامر الرابع ألا يحج بعد العام مشرك. 

فكانت هذه أربعة أمور بعث بها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم علي بن أبي طالب فبلغها عنه في الحج كله. وهكذا فيما فعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مواقفه.

وعن سؤال حول دور الخطاب الديني المعتدل للتقريب بين المسلمين وتعزيز اللحمة بينهم قال الشيخ:

بالنسبة لهذا الخطاب هو الخطاب المؤصل الذي يقوم على الكتاب والسنة، وهذا الذي ليس لأحد أن يرده من المسلمين، فكل المسلمين يقتنعون أن هذا الدين الموحد لهم يقوم على الرضى بالله ربا وبمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم رسولا وبالقرآن كتابا، فلا يختلفون على هذه الامور وإن اختلفوا فيما سوى ذلك من التفصيلات والجزئيات. 

فلذلك لا بد من التركيز على هذا الخطاب، ويركز عليه في المشاهد العامة كالحج وغيره.

وقد ذكرت تفريقا بيّنه عبد الرحمن بن عوف لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه عندما أراد أن يخطب في عرفه فبين للناس قضية السياسة والبيعة والاختيار. 

فقال له عبد الرحمن إنه يغلِب عليك رعاع الناس وإنهم سيطيرون بكلامك كل مطار، ولن ينزلوه منازله، فترك هذا الكلام حتى ترد إلى المدينة فتخلوَ بالمهاجرين والأنصار، فحينئذ قل ما شئت فسينزلونه منازله، ففعل ذلك عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه.
body_en:
His eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew said that the hajj has been bound up with politics ever since it was made obligatory, in the ninth year of the Hijrah, adding that the hajj is the largest conference that brings the Muslims together: the far and the near among them gather in it, their easterners and their westerners, their Arabs and their non-Arabs, meeting upon a word held in common — the word of God's oneness (tawḥīd), which unites the ranks of all the Muslims.

The Sheikh said, during an interview he gave today, Tuesday 15/10/2013, with the Al Jazeera satellite channel from the sacred site of Mina, that politics cannot be separated from the hajj under any circumstances; for it was during it that Sūrat Barāʾah was revealed, a sura filled with political rulings.

He explained that politics is of two kinds. One kind is part of the religion, and this is not separated from the hajj under any circumstances — such as the stands that God has commanded, for God the Exalted said {And co-operate in righteousness and God-consciousness, and do not co-operate in sin and transgression, and be conscious of God} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:2); and such as speaking about the liberation of the Aqsa Mosque, and about denouncing the genocide of the Syrian people, and other matters that are a position taken in the Sharia and at the same time a purely political position.

The other kind is negative, leading to disputes, quarrels and disorder among the Muslims in matters they have no need of; and this is what is to be avoided.

And this is the text of the Sheikh's interview:

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds; and may God bless and grant peace to our Prophet Muhammad, and to his family and all his Companions.

The hajj is the largest conference that brings the Muslims together: the far and the near among them gather in it, their easterners and their westerners, their Arabs and their non-Arabs, meeting upon a word held in common — the word of God's oneness, which unites the wool [ṣūf; read ṣufūf, "the ranks", as in the site's own summary above] of all the Muslims.

Politics is of two kinds. One kind is part of the religion, and this is not separated from the hajj under any circumstances — such as the stands that God has commanded, for God the Exalted said {And co-operate in righteousness and God-consciousness, and do not co-operate [in] sin and transgression, and be conscious of God} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:2); and such as speaking about the liberation of the Aqsa Mosque, and about denouncing the genocide of the Syrian people, and other matters that are a position taken in the Sharia and are at the same time a political position.

The other kind is negative, leading to disputes, quarrelling and disorder among the Muslims in matters they have no need of; and this is what is to be avoided.

For that reason the hajj has been bound up with politics ever since it was made obligatory. The hajj was made obligatory in the ninth year of the Hijrah, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Bakr al-Siddiq as commander over the hajj; then Sūrat Barāʾah was revealed, and it is all political rulings.

So the Messenger of God commanded Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, to proclaim on his behalf at the hajj. Ali went out in the wake of Abu Bakr, and proclaimed on behalf of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the sacred sites, and at ʿArafah, and at the Sacred House.

Ali, may God be pleased with him, was asked: with what did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, send you? He raised his hand and said: with four matters:

– The first matter, that none shall enter the Garden but a believing soul.

– The second matter, that no naked person shall circumambulate the House.

– The third matter, that whoever has a covenant between himself and the Messenger of God, his covenant [stands] to its term.

– The fourth matter, that no idolater shall perform the hajj after this year.

These were four matters with which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali ibn Abi Talib, and which he proclaimed on his behalf throughout the hajj. And so it is with what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did in the stands he took.

Asked about the role of moderate religious discourse in bringing the Muslims closer together and strengthening the bond between them, the Sheikh said:

As for this discourse, it is the well-grounded discourse that rests upon the Book and the Sunnah, and this is the one that no Muslim has any ground to reject. All the Muslims are convinced that this religion, which unites them, rests upon being content with God as Lord, with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Messenger, and with the Qur'an as Book. They do not differ over these matters, even if they differ over what lies beyond them, in the details and the particulars.

For that reason there must be a concentration upon this discourse, and it is to be concentrated upon at the public occasions, such as the hajj and others.

I have mentioned a distinction that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf set out for Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, when he wanted to preach at ʿArafah and to set out for the people the question of politics, of the pledge of allegiance and of the choosing [of a ruler].

Abd al-Rahman said to him: the rabble of the people prevail upon you, and they will scatter your words in every direction and will not put them in their proper places. So leave these words until you come back to Medina and are alone with the Emigrants and the Helpers; then say what you wish, and they will put it in its proper place. And Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, did that.

flags.arabic: وكالكلام عن تحرير المسجد الأقصى وعن إنكار الإبادة الجماعية للشعب السوري
flags.context: the examples of politics that is part of the religion, in both the summary and the verbatim interview
options: the liberation of the Aqsa Mosque, and denouncing the genocide of the Syrian people
the liberation of al-Masjid al-Aqsa, and condemnation of the genocide against the Syrian people
the freeing of the Aqsa Mosque, and repudiation of the mass killing of the Syrian people
flags.note: EDITORIAL, highest exposure in this record. These are the Sheikh's OWN words in the verbatim portion, not a reporter's paraphrase, spoken on Al Jazeera from Mina during the 2013 hajj. تحرير المسجد الأقصى ('the liberation of the Aqsa Mosque') and الإبادة الجماعية ('genocide', the standard Arabic rendering of the legal term) are both highly charged in English and in several Western jurisdictions, and the sentence places both inside a claim that such positions are religiously mandated at the hajj. Style guide section 6 forbids softening: 'genocide' has NOT been downgraded to 'mass killing', and 'liberation' has not been softened. Whether and how to publish is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office, not the translator.

flags.arabic: الموحدة لصفوف المسلمين جميعا (الملخص) / الموحدة لصوف المسلمين جميعا (نص المقابلة)
flags.context: the same sentence, in the site's summary and again in the verbatim transcript
options: reproduce both as printed and mark the transcript's word as a slip for ṣufūf
harmonise the transcript to the summary
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11). The record prints the same sentence twice. The summary has صفوف ('the ranks'), the transcript صوف ('wool'), which is meaningless here. Both are preserved in body_ar; the English marks the transcript's word in brackets rather than silently repairing it. This is one of FOUR places where the summary and the transcript of the same sentence diverge; see the separate flag.

flags.arabic: {وتعاونوا على البر والتقوى ولا تعاونوا الإثم والعدوان واتقوا الله}
flags.context: the Qur'anic quotation as it appears in the verbatim transcript
options: mark the supplied preposition in brackets and flag the lacuna
print the verse as the summary has it, with على
print the transcript's wording untouched
flags.note: MISSING WORD IN QUOTED SCRIPTURE (house rule 11). The transcript drops على from ولا تعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:2); the summary a few lines earlier has it. Arabic cannot show that absence in English without help, so the English marks the supplied element as 'do not co-operate [in] sin and transgression'. The text has NOT been restored from memory in body_ar, and the verse is not written out anywhere in full in the Sheikh's own voice. Qur'anic renderings in this corpus are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

flags.arabic: من كان بينه وبين رسول الله عهد فعهده إلا مدته
flags.context: the third of the four matters Ali proclaimed
options: his covenant [stands] to its term (reading إلا as إلى)
his covenant is [honoured] until its term
reproduce the source's wording and leave it unresolved
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11), inside a quotation of a Companion's proclamation. إلا ('except') gives no sense; the known wording is فعهده إلى مدته, 'his covenant stands to its term', which is also the sense required by Sūrat Barāʾah. Translated by the evident sense, with the supplied verb bracketed; body_ar preserves the source. Not restored silently.

flags.arabic: لا يدخل الجنة إلا نفس مؤمنة / فخرج في علي في أثر أبي بكر
flags.context: the first of the four matters, and the sentence introducing Ali's departure
options: reproduce both as printed and record the variants
correct them to the familiar wordings
flags.note: SOURCE, recorded not corrected. (1) The best-known wording of the first proclamation is 'none shall enter the Garden but a MUSLIM soul' (نفس مسلمة); the record has مؤمنة, 'believing'. The Sheikh gives no collection and no grading for the report, so none has been added, and the variant has not been normalised. (2) فخرج في علي contains an intrusive في; translated as if 'Ali went out'.

flags.arabic: الملخص الصحفي يكرر نص المقابلة مع اختلافات
flags.context: the relation between the first four paragraphs and the transcript that follows
options: keep both, translate both, and record the four divergences
keep only the verbatim transcript
keep only the summary
flags.note: STRUCTURE. This record is a site news summary followed by 'And this is the text of the Sheikh's interview', after which two of the summary's paragraphs are repeated verbatim — but not identically. The four divergences are: صفوف / صوف; the Qur'anic على present / absent; بحت ('purely' political) present in the summary and absent from the transcript; and النزاعات / النزاع. In every case the SUMMARY is the better-formed text and the TRANSCRIPT is the one presented as the Sheikh's own words, which is the wrong way round. Both are translated in full, neither is deduplicated, and the site should not silently show only one.

flags.arabic: وهي في نفس الوقت موقف سياسي بحت (الملخص) / وهي في نفس الموقت موقف سياسي (النص)
flags.context: the characterisation of religiously mandated political stands
options: reproduce both, keeping 'purely' only where the source has بحت
carry 'purely' into both
flags.note: The reporter's summary calls such stands 'a purely political position' (موقف سياسي بحت); the verbatim transcript says only 'a political position', and also misspells الوقت as الموقت. The intensifier has NOT been carried into the transcript, since the whole point of a verbatim section is that it is what he said. Style guide section 6: never strengthen.

flags.arabic: تفريقا بيّنه عبد الرحمن بن عوف لعمر بن الخطاب … إنه يغلِب عليك رعاع الناس
flags.context: the closing account, on where political speech belongs
options: a distinction that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf set out for Umar ibn al-Khattab
a distinction Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf made clear to Umar
flags.note: The account is the one in al-Bukhari in which Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf dissuades Umar from addressing the question of the succession at the hajj; the Sheikh gives no attribution and none has been added. Its function in the interview is important and should not be lost: he uses it to distinguish political speech that belongs at the hajj from political speech that does not — which qualifies everything said earlier about politics and the hajj. Any excerpt that drops this paragraph misrepresents the interview.

flags.context: the CMS timestamp on the record
options: treat as the date the item was uploaded to the CMS
treat as the date of composition
flags.note: CORPUS-WIDE DEFECT. The CMS serves a bulk-upload timestamp, not the date the Sheikh spoke or wrote. date_is_cms_upload is set true. Where the body itself names a date, that internal date is the better evidence and is kept in the English.

translator_notes: Two texts in one record: a site news summary, then the verbatim transcript of the Sheikh's Al Jazeera interview from Mina. The English keeps them distinct, and the bilingual display must do the same, because only the second is his own wording.
كلمة سواء ('a word held in common') echoes Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:64; the source neither quotes nor cites it, so no reference has been added.
سورة براءة is the alternative name of Sūrat al-Tawbah; the source's name is kept. The first occurrence in the summary is spelt براءه, in the transcript براءة; both preserved in body_ar.
فُرض / منذ فرضه is the passive of farḍ and is rendered 'was made obligatory', consistent with the fixed mapping.
الرضى بالله ربا وبمحمد رسولا وبالقرآن كتابا echoes a well-known prophetic formula on the taste of faith; rendered plainly, with no attribution added.
المهاجرين والأنصار are rendered by the conventional 'the Emigrants and the Helpers'.
مشعر منى: Mina is one of the mashāʿir, the ritual sites of the hajj; 'the sacred site of Mina'.
